headline: Recycling transforms waste into resources—what's finished in one form can begin again in another
universal_truth: Endings can be beginnings; waste in one context is raw material in another; reuse multiplies value
fun_facts: Aluminum can be recycled indefinitely without losing quality—the same atoms become can after can
Recycling one ton of paper saves 17 trees and 7,000 gallons of water
Your body recycles atoms constantly—most of you is replaced every few years
discussion_questions: What in your life could be recycled or repurposed?
Where do you throw away what could have value elsewhere?
What 'waste' experience could become raw material for something new?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: That aluminum can becomes a new can. That old essay becomes fuel for a better one. Recycling isn't just environmental—it's a mindset. What seems finished often contains raw material for the next thing.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often discard things when their first use ends. But 'waste' is just unused potential. How do we see resources where others see trash?

options.text: Recycling requires recognizing that materials retain value beyond their original form—seeing the resource within the 'waste'
options.response: Yes. Recycling is an act of perception—seeing the aluminum in the can, the insight in the failure, the opportunity in the ending. Value persists through form changes.
Practically yes, but conceptually it requires seeing value where others see waste...

q1.title: Material Cycles
q1.script: Atoms don't disappear—they transform. The carbon in your body was once in plants, animals, rocks, atmosphere. Everything cycles. Recycling just speeds up what nature does anyway.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Material Cycles"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Waste as Resource
q2.script: One industry's waste is another's raw material. Sawdust becomes particle board. Food scraps become compost. Seeing waste as misplaced resource opens possibilities.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Experience Recycling
q3.script: Failed projects contain lessons. Old skills transfer to new domains. Difficult experiences become stories that help others. You can recycle experiences too—nothing is wasted if you extract the value.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Endings can be beginnings. Waste in one context is raw material in another. Learn to recycle—materials, ideas, and experiences.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 233. Tomorrow, we'll explore when stuff ends up wrong—errors and mistakes. Until then, identify something you could recycle or repurpose.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Resource Recovery - What Can You Reuse?
growTrack.activity: What have you recently finished, discarded, or abandoned? A project, a skill, an experience? What raw material does it contain for something new? Failed projects have lessons. Old skills transfer. Nothing is truly wasted if you extract value.
